items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: He was with Alfred Newman for many years.

ctx.x: No, I was the world's worst musician. That's why I quit. But I'm glad to know about your family background.

Well, my father was a musician, my brother was the greatest drummer I ever lived. He was with Alfred Newman for many years. And Hollywood. I have the red book that Soussone got out, it says that he played in the pit at the Orphiom and with his brother Johnny's band. He was the greatest woodpile man on the Pacific coast. You know the woodpile, the marimbas, huh? And he had Georgia the drum section. He made enough money to retire in three figures. He had the drawing account $15,000 a year if he never had a note.…
I didn't know he was a trombonist.

items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: He had to read to play with Alfred Newman, you know.

ctx.x: So a lady said to me, are you Jewish?

I said, no. She said, well your brother called you Simon. He says, Jewish. I said, he calls me lots of things. I said, but I'm not Jewish, you know what I mean? But he was funny. He was the best company in the world. But he used to break up that band. He's the first one that I ever heard take a half a chorus on the drums. They didn't feature the drums much in the old days, you know. No. No. But he'd play on the rim and on the floor and everything. I understand when he played first trumpet, I mean played drums at…
You know, it's now five o'clock and I've got to close up and I've got to rule.
